# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `pixi run gen-command-docs` from src/wgsextract_cli/commands/registry.py (tiers, journeys, deprecations), _help_catalog.py (examples, outputs) and _command_needs.py (tools, run time). Don't edit by hand. -->

Commands are grouped by tier. The core tier is the usual path, in order: check a file, make microarray files or find haplogroups, extract reads, (re)align, call and annotate variants, then summarise them in a report. Outputs go to the output directory (`--outdir`, the configured `outdir` or the `--genome` folder) unless noted; a run that registers outputs also writes a `.manifest.json` beside its main output. Run `wgsextract help <command>` for its options (`--help-all` adds the advanced ones) and `wgsextract help --all --json` for every command's options as JSON. *Needs* lists the external tools a command checks for (`wgsextract deps check` shows which are installed) and how long it typically takes.

## Start from what you have

- **Nothing yet (a first run):** `deps check` (check that the external tools are installed) → `ref bootstrap` (download the small shared files, e.g. liftover chains) → `ref library` (download a reference genome) → `example-genome download` (get a public example genome to practise on)
- **A BAM or CRAM from a sequencing service (Nebula, Dante Labs, Sequencing.com, ...):** `info` (check the reference build, file health and coverage) → `microarray` (make 23andMe/AncestryDNA-style files to upload) → `lineage y-haplogroup` (find the paternal haplogroup) → `lineage mt-haplogroup` (find the maternal haplogroup) → `vcf snp` (call SNPs into a VCF) → `vep run` (predict each variant's effect on genes) → `report` (summarise everything in one HTML report)
- **A BAM or CRAM on the wrong build (hg19 when you want hg38, or the reverse):** `info` (see which build it is) → `realign` (re-map it to the other build) → `info` (check the new file, then continue as above)
- **FASTQ files (raw reads):** `align` (map the reads to a reference, making a BAM/CRAM) → `info` (check the result, then continue as for a BAM/CRAM)
- **A VCF (from a provider or another pipeline):** `vcf clinvar` (add ClinVar clinical significance) → `vcf filter` (keep a gene, region or quality range) → `vep run` (predict each variant's effect on genes) → `vcf table` (one row per variant, for spreadsheets and SQL)
- **A consumer raw-data file (23andMe, AncestryDNA, ...):** `info chip` (identify the vendor, chip and revision)

## Start here, in this order

| Command | What it does | Writes | Needs | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | Check a BAM/CRAM: reference build, file health, coverage. | Prints a summary and caches it as &lt;input file name>.wgse_info.json; with --format also &lt;input file name>_chromosomes and _qc (QC stats) as .tsv or .parquet. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; seconds on a 30x genome | `wgsextract info --input sample.cram` |
| `info calculate-coverage` | Generate a full breadth-of-coverage report. | &lt;input file name>_coverage.tsv, or with --bins &lt;input file name>_coverage_bins.tsv (depth bands, or .parquet with --format parquet) instead. With --by, &lt;input>_&lt;bed>_target_coverage.tsv (depth per target) and &lt;input>_&lt;bed>_target_summary.txt (on- and off-target depth, enrichment and targets below --min-depth). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract info calculate-coverage --input sample.cram` |
| `info coverage-sample` | Quickly estimate per-chromosome breadth of coverage by sampling ~1,000 evenly spaced, length-weighted 1 kb windows. | &lt;input file name>_samplecvg.json; a whole-file run also updates the info cache. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract info coverage-sample --input sample.cram` |
| `info chip` | Identify the vendor, chip and revision of a consumer microarray raw-data file (23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage, FTDNA, ...) from its header and marker set, with a confidence score and the matching --formats template. | Prints the vendor, chip and matching --formats template; writes no files. | no external tools; seconds for a raw-data file | `wgsextract info chip --input genome_raw_data.txt` |
| `microarray` | Make 23andMe/AncestryDNA-style raw-data files to upload. | &lt;input stem>_&lt;format>.txt (or the vendor's extension) per format, such as sample_23andMe_V5.txt, and &lt;input stem>_CombinedKit.txt; with --format also &lt;input stem>_genotypes.tsv or .parquet. | bcftools, bgzip, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract microarray --input sample.cram --formats 23andme_v5` |
| `lineage y-haplogroup` | Predict paternal haplogroups with native Yleaf-derived analysis (BAM/CRAM/VCF). | yleaf/: hg_prediction.hg, the per-sample .out/.fmf/.info reports and run.json; prints the haplogroup and the tree's name and version. | bcftools, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract lineage y-haplogroup --input sample.cram` |
| `lineage y-str` | Count Y-STR repeats (FamilyTreeDNA Y-12 to Y-111, PowerPlex Y23, Yfiler Plus) from a BAM/CRAM for genealogy matching. | ystr/: &lt;sample>.ystr.tsv, &lt;sample>.ftdna.csv (FTDNA marker order) and run.json. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract lineage y-str --input sample.cram --panel Y-37` |
| `lineage mt-haplogroup` | Predict your maternal haplogroup using Haplogrep 3, optionally checking mtDNA contamination with haplocheck. | haplogrep_results.txt; prints the mtDNA haplogroup and Haplogrep 3 tree. With --contamination, also haplocheck_contamination.txt (+ .raw.txt, .html). | bcftools, haplogrep3, java, samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl, haplocheck, tabix; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract lineage mt-haplogroup --input sample.cram` |
| `extract mito-fasta` | Extract the Mitochondrial DNA (chrM) consensus sequence. | &lt;input stem>_MT.fasta: the mtDNA consensus sequence. | bcftools, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract mito-fasta --input sample.cram` |
| `extract mito-vcf` | Call variants specifically for the mitochondrial DNA. | &lt;input stem>_MT.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract mito-vcf --input sample.cram` |
| `extract mt-bam` | Isolate all mitochondrial-related reads into a new, smaller BAM file. | &lt;input stem>_mtDNA.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract mt-bam --input sample.cram` |
| `extract ydna-bam` | Extract all Y-chromosome reads into a separate BAM file. | &lt;input stem>_Y.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract ydna-bam --input sample.cram` |
| `extract ydna-vcf` | Call variants specifically for the Y-chromosome. | &lt;input stem>_Y.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, bgzip, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract ydna-vcf --input sample.cram` |
| `extract y-mt-extract` | Extract both Y-chromosome and Mitochondrial reads into a single, combined BAM file. | &lt;input stem>_Y_MT.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract y-mt-extract --input sample.cram` |
| `extract unmapped` | Extract reads that did not align to the reference. | &lt;input stem>_unmapped.bam (+ .bai); FASTQ files with --fastq. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract unmapped --input sample.cram` |
| `extract custom` | Extract reads from a specific chromosomal region or gene of interest. | &lt;input stem>_&lt;region>.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract custom --input sample.cram --region chr17:43044295-43125483` |
| `realign` | Re-map a BAM/CRAM to another build, e.g. hg19 to hg38. | &lt;input stem>_aligned.bam or .cram (+ index); with --keep-fastq, also &lt;input stem>_R1/_R2.fastq.gz (single-end ONT/PacBio: &lt;input stem>.fastq.gz). Completed steps are recorded in &lt;output>.steps.json, so a rerun resumes after a crash. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, bgzip, bwa, bwa-mem2, curl, gatk, minimap2, pbmm2, sambamba, samblaster; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract realign --input sample_hg19.bam --ref hs38.fa` |
| `align` | Map raw FASTQ reads to a reference, making a BAM/CRAM. | &lt;reads stem>_aligned.bam or .cram (+ index). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, bwa, bwa-mem2, curl, gatk, minimap2, pbmm2, sambamba, samblaster; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract align --r1 sample_R1.fastq.gz --r2 sample_R2.fastq.gz --ref hs38.fa` |
| `vcf snp` | Call Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) using bcftools. | snps.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf snp --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf indel` | Call Small Insertions and Deletions (InDels) using bcftools. | indels.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf indel --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf annotate` | Add external metadata (like population frequencies or disease risk) to your VCF file. | annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf annotate --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --ann-vcf dbsnp.vcf.gz --cols ID` |
| `vcf filter` | Filter your results. | filtered.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf filter --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --expr 'QUAL>30'` |
| `vcf table` | Export variants and their annotations (gene, consequence, ClinVar, gnomAD, genotype, depth, ...) as one row per variant, in a TSV (or Parquet) table and an SQLite database to query. | &lt;input stem>_variants.tsv (or .parquet with --format parquet) and &lt;input stem>_variants.sqlite: one row per variant allele, with its annotations. | bcftools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, tabix; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf table --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf clinvar` | Annotate VCF with ClinVar pathogenicity data. | clinvar_annotated.vcf.gz and clinvar_pathogenic.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf clinvar --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf revel` | Annotate VCF with REVEL pathogenicity scores. | revel_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --min-score N, also revel_gt_N.vcf.gz. | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf revel --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf gnomad` | Annotate VCF with gnomAD population frequencies. | gnomad_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --max-af AF, also gnomad_af_lt_AF.vcf.gz and its .confidence.tsv table. | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf gnomad --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --max-af 0.01` |
| `vcf pharmgkb` | Annotate VCF with PharmGKB drug metabolism data. | pharmgkb_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf pharmgkb --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vep download` | Download the VEP cache (standard GRCh37/38) to your local machine for faster, offline annotation. | Into the VEP cache directory (vep_cache, or --vep-cache). | curl, tar; depends on download speed | `wgsextract vep download --assembly GRCh38` |
| `vep verify` | Check your existing VEP cache for missing files or corruption. | Prints what is missing or damaged; writes no files. | no external tools; seconds | `wgsextract vep verify --assembly GRCh38` |
| `vep run` | Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor. | &lt;input stem>_vep.vcf.gz (or .tsv/.json with --format), with VEP's summary. | bcftools, tabix, vep; depending on options and inputs, also: samtools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vep run --input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `report` | Summarise a sample's results in one local HTML report. | &lt;sample>_personal_report.html, .md and .json and &lt;sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv (or .parquet with --format parquet) in the sample folder (or --outdir); evidence links are relative to the sample folder. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; seconds from existing results | `wgsextract report --genome HG002` |

## Setup

| Command | What it does | Writes | Needs | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref aadr` | Explicitly fetch the hash-pinned CC0 AADR v66.p1 2M SNP panel. | Into the reference library (reflib): the AADR 2M SNP panel. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref aadr --install` |
| `ref ybrowse` | Explicitly install a hash-pinned, sites-only GRCh38 yBrowse snapshot. | Into the reference library (reflib): the yBrowse GRCh38 SNP sites. | bgzip, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref ybrowse --install` |
| `ref download` | Download a reference FASTA from a URL (--url) to a path (--out). | The FASTA at --out. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref download --url https://example.org/genome.fa.gz --out genome.fa.gz` |
| `ref index` | Prepare a FASTA file for use by indexing it. | Beside the FASTA: .fai, .dict and the aligner's index files. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bwa, bwa-mem2, curl; hours, once per reference | `wgsextract ref index --ref hs38.fa` |
| `ref count-ns` | Calculate the percentage of 'N' (unknown) bases in a genome. | &lt;reference stem>_ncnt.csv and &lt;reference stem>_nbin.csv. | no external tools; minutes, once per reference | `wgsextract ref count-ns --ref hs38.fa` |
| `ref verify` | Ensure your reference genome file isn't corrupted and has all the necessary companion files (indexes, dicts). | Prints what is missing or damaged; creates a missing .fai (and .gzi for a compressed FASTA) beside the FASTA. | samtools; minutes, once per reference | `wgsextract ref verify --ref hs38.fa` |
| `ref library` | Opens the interactive reference manager to help you organize and download genomic data. | Into the reference library (reflib): the chosen reference genome and its indexes. | bcftools, bgzip, curl, htsfile, samtools, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref library --list` |
| `ref status` | Report reference library asset status. | Prints the reference library's status; writes no files. | no external tools; seconds | `wgsextract ref status` |
| `ref gene-map` | Download or delete lightweight gene-to-coordinate mapping files (hg19/hg38), enabling you to filter VCFs by gene name (e.g. BRCA1). | Into the reference library (reflib): the hg19 and hg38 gene maps (--delete removes them). | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref gene-map` |
| `ref clinvar` | Download official ClinVar VCF for hg19 and hg38. | Into the reference library (reflib): ClinVar VCFs for hg19 and hg38. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref clinvar` |
| `ref revel` | Download REVEL pathogenicity scores for hg19 and hg38. | Into the reference library (reflib): REVEL score files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref revel` |
| `ref phylop` | Download UCSC's PhyloP 100-way conservation scores (~10 GB bigWig). | Into the reference library (reflib): the PhyloP bigWig. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref phylop --build hg38` |
| `ref gnomad` | Download gnomAD population allele frequencies. | Into the reference library (reflib): gnomAD allele-frequency files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref gnomad` |
| `ref spliceai` | Download SpliceAI scores for hg38 (Ensembl, MANE SNVs); index a manual hg19 download. | Into the reference library (reflib): SpliceAI score files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref spliceai` |
| `ref alphamissense` | Download AlphaMissense scores for hg19 and hg38. | Into the reference library (reflib): AlphaMissense score files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref alphamissense` |
| `ref pharmgkb` | Download PharmGKB annotations. | Into the reference library (reflib): PharmGKB annotation files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, curl, tabix; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref pharmgkb` |
| `ref cadd` | Download CADD v1.7 deleteriousness scores (all possible SNVs plus gnomAD indels, ~85 GB per build) with their tabix indexes. | Into the reference library (reflib): CADD score files and tabix indexes. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref cadd --build hg38` |
| `ref gerp` | Download GERP++ conservation scores as a bigWig (hg38 from Ensembl, ~9.6 GB; hg19 from UCSC, ~7.6 GB). | Into the reference library (reflib): the GERP++ bigWig. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref gerp --build hg38` |
| `ref bootstrap` | Download and initialize the reference library bootstrap (VCFs, chains, etc.). | Into the reference library (reflib): the bootstrap VCFs, liftover chains and other small files. | no external tools; depends on download speed | `wgsextract ref bootstrap` |
| `deps check` | Verify that all required bioinformatics tools (samtools, bcftools, etc.) are installed and accessible in your system path. | Prints each tool's status; writes no files. | no external tools; seconds | `wgsextract deps check` |
| `example-genome list` | List curated 1000 Genomes examples. | Prints the curated examples; writes no files. | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract example-genome list` |
| `example-genome download` | Download curated 1000 Genomes examples into the genome library. | Into &lt;genome_library>/test-1000genomes/&lt;example id>/, with a genome config file. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: curl; depends on download speed | `wgsextract example-genome download na12878-lowcov-bam` |
| `sample show` | Show the sample's overrides, the facts commands detected from each of its files (with method, confidence and date) and its recorded results. | Prints the sample's overrides, recorded facts and results; writes no files. | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract sample show --genome HG002` |
| `sample set` | Set an override (--sex, --platform) that commands use instead of what they detect: a sex for the whole genome folder, else for --input alone. | wgsextract.sample.toml in the sample folder (the --genome folder, --workspace or the input's folder). | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract sample set --genome HG002 --sex Female` |
| `sample unset` | Remove an override so commands detect that fact again: the folder-wide one and, with --input, that file's own. | wgsextract.sample.toml in the sample folder. | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract sample unset --genome HG002 --sex` |
| `config` | Show the settings in use and the config.toml path. | Prints the settings; in a terminal, offers to create a default config.toml. | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract config` |
| `report-issue` | Report a problem: a redacted, pre-filled GitHub bug report. | Prints a redacted bug report and its GitHub link and saves the report as issue-report-&lt;time>.md in state/reports (setting state_directory); opens the browser only after you agree or with --open. | no external tools; seconds | `wgsextract report-issue` |
| `help` | List every command, or explain one: 'help vcf snp'. | Prints to stdout; writes no files. | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract help --all` |

## Advanced

| Command | What it does | Writes | Needs | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extract bam-subset` | Create a smaller version of your BAM file using a random fraction of reads (e.g. 0.1 for 10%). | &lt;input stem>_subset.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract extract bam-subset --input sample.cram --fraction 0.1` |
| `vcf to-fasta` | Build your personal consensus genome: the reference FASTA with your variants applied (heterozygous SNVs as IUPAC codes by default), and N where a gVCF has no call. | &lt;input stem>_consensus.fa.gz (+ .fai); with --chain, a .chain file. | bcftools, bgzip, samtools, tabix; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf to-fasta --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --ref hs38.fa` |
| `vcf trio` | Analyze inheritance patterns. | trio_&lt;mode>.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); from alignments, also trio_joint.vcf.gz (and trio_denovo_isolated.vcf.gz for --mode denovo). The manifest is trio.manifest.json. | bcftools, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf trio --proband child.vcf.gz --mother mother.vcf.gz --father father.vcf.gz --mode denovo` |
| `vcf cnv` | Call Copy Number Variants (CNVs) using Delly. | cnv.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, delly, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf cnv --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf sv` | Call Structural Variants (SVs) using Delly for short reads, Sniffles for Nanopore (ONT, auto-detected) or other long reads, or pbsv/Sniffles for PacBio. | sv.vcf.gz (Delly), pbsv.vcf.gz or sniffles.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: delly, pbsv, sniffles; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf sv --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf freebayes` | A Bayesian genetic variant detector. | freebayes.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, freebayes, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf freebayes --input sample.cram --region chr20` |
| `vcf gatk` | Industry-standard GATK HaplotypeCaller. | gatk.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | gatk, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf gatk --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf deepvariant` | Google's Deep Variant variant caller. | deepvariant.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) and deepvariant.vcf.gz.steps.json; until it finishes, the stages' work in .deepvariant.work, where a rerun resumes. | samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, docker, run_deepvariant, sambamba; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf deepvariant --input sample.cram` |
| `vcf clair3` | Clair3 small-variant caller for Oxford Nanopore reads (optional; Linux x86-64 only, install with `pixi install -e clair3`). | clair3.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, run_clair3.sh, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf clair3 --input ont.bam` |
| `vcf phase` | Phase a sample's heterozygous calls with its reads (WhatsHap, or LongPhase for Nanopore and PacBio), and optionally tag the reads by haplotype. | phased.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) and phased.blocks.tsv; with --haplotag, haplotagged.bam or .cram (+ index). | bcftools, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: longphase, whatshap; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf phase --input ont.bam --vcf-input clair3.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf phylop` | Annotate VCF with PhyloP conservation scores. | phylop_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --min-score N, also phylop_gt_N.vcf.gz. | bcftools, bgzip, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf phylop --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf cadd` | Annotate VCF with CADD deleteriousness scores (CADD_RAW, CADD_PHRED). | cadd_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --min-score N, also cadd_gt_N.vcf.gz. | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf cadd --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --min-score 20` |
| `vcf gerp` | Annotate VCF with GERP++ conservation scores (GERP). | gerp_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --min-score N, also gerp_gt_N.vcf.gz. | bcftools, bgzip, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf gerp --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf spliceai` | Annotate VCF with SpliceAI splicing scores. | spliceai_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf spliceai --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf alphamissense` | Annotate VCF with AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores. | alphamissense_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi); with --min-score N, also alphamissense_gt_N.vcf.gz. | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf alphamissense --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf pharmcat` | Call star-allele diplotypes and drug-response phenotypes (CYP2C19, CYP2C9, DPYD, ...) with PharmCAT, and write its prescribing report. | &lt;stem>.report.html and &lt;stem>.phenotype.json from PharmCAT. | bcftools, pharmcat, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf pharmcat --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `vcf chain-annotate` | Sequentially apply multiple annotations to a single VCF. | chain_annotated.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bgzip, samtools, vep; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract vcf chain-annotate --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz --annotations clinvar,gnomad` |
| `bam sort` | Sort alignments by genomic coordinates. | &lt;input stem>_sorted.bam or .cram (+ index). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam sort --input sample.bam` |
| `bam index` | Create a random-access index (.bai/.crai) for your file. | Beside the input: &lt;input>.bai or .crai. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam index --input sample.bam` |
| `bam unindex` | Remove the index file associated with your BAM/CRAM. | Deletes the input's .bai/.crai index; writes no files. | samtools; instant | `wgsextract bam unindex --input sample.bam` |
| `bam unsort` | Mark the file as 'unsorted' in the header. | &lt;input stem>_unsorted.bam or .cram. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam unsort --input sample.bam` |
| `bam to-cram` | Convert BAM to the modern CRAM format. | &lt;input stem>.cram (+ .crai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam to-cram --input sample.bam --ref hs38.fa` |
| `bam to-bam` | Convert a CRAM file back to the traditional BAM format. | &lt;input stem>.bam (+ .bai). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, sambamba; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam to-bam --input sample.cram` |
| `bam unalign` | Extract raw reads from a BAM/CRAM back into FASTQ format. | The FASTQ files named by --r1/--r2 (or --se). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam unalign --input sample.cram --r1 sample_R1.fastq.gz --r2 sample_R2.fastq.gz` |
| `bam identify` | Analyze your BAM header to determine exactly which reference genome was used for the original alignment. | Prints the reference the file was aligned to; writes no files. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; seconds | `wgsextract bam identify --input sample.bam` |
| `bam merge` | Merge several coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files (e.g. per-lane files) aligned to the same reference into one indexed file. | merged.bam or merged.cram (+ index), or the --output path; each run keeps its own read group under one sample name (SM). | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam merge lane1.bam lane2.bam --output sample.bam` |
| `bam to-ubam` | Convert an aligned BAM/CRAM or FASTQ reads into a queryname-sorted unaligned BAM (uBAM) for GATK pipelines. | &lt;input stem>_unaligned.bam: queryname-sorted unaligned reads. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract bam to-ubam --input sample.cram` |
| `qc fastp` | An ultra-fast all-in-one pre-processor. | &lt;stem>_fp_1.fastq.gz (and _fp_2), &lt;stem>_fastp.html and &lt;stem>_fastp.json. | fastp; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract qc fastp --r1 sample_R1.fastq.gz --r2 sample_R2.fastq.gz` |
| `qc fastqc` | The industry-standard quality check for raw reads. | FastQC's &lt;input>_fastqc.html and .zip. | fastqc; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract qc fastqc --input sample_R1.fastq.gz` |
| `qc multiqc` | Combine existing FastQC reports, bcftools stats and WGS Extract result manifests into one local HTML report. | multiqc_report.html, in --outdir, else in the --input directory (or beside an --input file). | multiqc; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, fastqc; seconds | `wgsextract qc multiqc --input fastqc_reports/` |
| `qc multiqc-metrics` | Write MultiQC custom-content files (wgsextract_*_mqc.json) from result manifests; MultiQC isn't needed. | wgsextract_*_mqc.json MultiQC custom-content files, in --outdir, else in the --input directory (or beside an --input file). | no external tools; seconds | `wgsextract qc multiqc-metrics --input results/` |
| `qc vcf` | Generate statistical reports for your VCF file to check the quality and distribution of your variant calls. | &lt;input file name>.vcfstats.txt (e.g. sample.vcf.gz.vcfstats.txt), in --outdir, else beside the input. | bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract qc vcf --vcf-input sample.vcf.gz` |
| `qc fake-data` | Generate fake BAM, CRAM, VCF, and FASTQ files for testing. | fake.cram, fake.bam, fake.vcf or fake_R1/_R2.fastq.gz, and the fake reference. | bcftools, bgzip, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: sambamba; seconds for small inputs | `wgsextract qc fake-data --outdir out/fake --type bam,vcf --seed 1` |
| `repair ftdna-bam` | Fix formatting errors specific to Family Tree DNA (FTDNA) BAM files that cause them to fail in standard tools like GATK. | &lt;input stem>_repaired.bam (+ .bai), or the --output path. | samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract repair ftdna-bam --input ftdna.bam` |
| `repair ftdna-vcf` | Fix formatting errors in FTDNA VCF files to make them compatible with modern annotation tools like VEP. | &lt;input stem>_repaired.vcf, or the --output path. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; seconds | `wgsextract repair ftdna-vcf --input ftdna.vcf` |
| `analyze comprehensive` | Run a full-chain analysis: QC, lineage, variant calling, annotation, and significant variant filtering. | The QC, lineage, variant and annotation outputs of each step, and a summary; analyze.steps.json records the completed steps. | bcftools, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract analyze comprehensive --input sample.cram` |
| `analyze batch-gen` | Generate a batch configuration file from a directory of genomes. | A batch CSV/TSV for 'analyze comprehensive --batch' (--output). | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract analyze batch-gen --directory genomes/ --output batch.tsv` |
| `typing cyp2d6` | Call CYP2D6 star alleles, including copy-number and hybrid alleles, with Cyrius, and write a PharmCAT outside call. | Cyrius's &lt;stem>.json/.tsv and &lt;stem>.cyp2d6.pharmcat.tsv. | cyrius, minimap2, samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract typing cyp2d6 --input sample.cram` |
| `typing hla` | Call HLA class I and II alleles with T1K from reads in the MHC, and write a PharmCAT outside call for HLA-A/HLA-B. | &lt;stem>.t1k_genotype.tsv (and T1K's other files) and &lt;stem>.hla.pharmcat.tsv. | run-t1k, samtools, t1k-build.pl; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract typing hla --input sample.cram` |
| `typing str` | Size the disease-causing repeats of ExpansionHunter's catalog (HTT, FMR1, C9ORF72, ...) and flag those outside STRchive's normal range. | ExpansionHunter's &lt;stem>.str.vcf/.json and a flagged-repeat summary. | ExpansionHunter, samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; minutes on a 30x genome | `wgsextract typing str --input sample.cram` |
| `methylation pileup` | Tabulate 5mC (and optionally 5hmC) per CpG with modkit into a bedMethyl file and summary. | &lt;input stem>.&lt;context>.bedmethyl.gz (+ .tbi) and &lt;input stem>.&lt;context>.methylation.tsv; with --format parquet the summary is .methylation.parquet and the calls are also in &lt;input stem>.&lt;context>.bedmethyl.parquet. | modkit, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract methylation pileup --input ont.bam` |
| `basecall` | Nanopore POD5 signal to reads with Dorado (optional). | &lt;POD5 file or folder stem>.&lt;model>[.&lt;modifications>][.subset].bam: unaligned reads with Dorado's tags (MM/ML with --modified-bases), beside the POD5 input or in --outdir. | dorado, samtools; hours for a MinION flow cell on a GPU | `wgsextract basecall --input pod5/ --modified-bases 5mCG_5hmCG` |
| `panel bed` | Write a BED of gene regions for Nanopore adaptive sampling (MinKNOW) or targeted analysis: genes and presets are padded (default 100 kb each side), clipped and merged, from the bundled NCBI RefSeq annotations of hg38, T2T or hg19. | panel_&lt;presets>[_&lt;genes>]_&lt;build>_pad&lt;N>kb.bed, the genes named when up to three, else &lt;N>genes-&lt;digest> (BED4: contig, start, end, genes; contig names from --ref when given). | no external tools; instant | `wgsextract panel bed --preset pharmacogenes` |
| `pet-align` | Align and call variants for a cat or dog genome. | &lt;reads stem>_&lt;species>.bam or .cram (+ index) and &lt;reads stem>_&lt;species>.vcf.gz (+ .tbi). | bcftools, bwa, samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bwa-mem2, sambamba, samblaster; hours on a 30x genome | `wgsextract pet-align --r1 dog_R1.fastq.gz --r2 dog_R2.fastq.gz --species dog` |
| `sign create` | Hash files or directories into a sha256sum-compatible SHA256SUMS manifest, signed with ssh-keygen when a key is given. | SHA256SUMS in the inputs' folder (or --output); SHA256SUMS.sig with --key. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: ssh-keygen; minutes for genome-sized files | `wgsextract sign create results/` |
| `sign verify` | Check a SHA256SUMS manifest's OpenSSH signature against a trusted key, then re-hash every listed file. | Prints the verification result; writes no files. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: ssh-keygen; minutes for genome-sized files | `wgsextract sign verify results/SHA256SUMS --public-key key.pub` |
| `benchmark` | Time the main workflows on test data. | runs/&lt;timestamp>/ under --outdir (default out/benchmark): benchmark_report.md and benchmark_results.json (timings, tool versions) and per-step logs. | no external tools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, bgzip, curl, samtools, tabix; hours for the full suite | `wgsextract benchmark --profile smoke` |
| `serve` | Local HTTP/JSON and MCP server for apps and AI agents. | Prints the server's address and token, also saved to state/server/server.json (setting state_directory) for you only; jobs and their logs go in state/server/jobs. Each operation writes its usual outputs and result manifest. | no external tools; seconds to start; runs until stopped | `wgsextract serve --allow ~/wgs` |

## Deprecated

These still work for one more minor release, with a warning (`deprecated_command`).

| Command | Use instead | Removed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vep` without a subcommand | `vep run` | 0.8.0 |
| `ref library-list` | `ref library --list` | 0.8.0 |

## Help topics

`wgsextract help <topic>` explains:

- `references`: Reference genomes: what they are, where they come from.
- `builds`: Genome builds (hg19, hg38, T2T) and moving between them.
- `genome-library`: Keep each person's files in a folder; select it with --genome.
- `coverage`: Coverage and depth, and the low-depth warnings.
- `exit-codes`: What wgsextract's exit codes mean.
- `manifests`: The result manifest each run writes, and --json.
- `privacy`: Your genome is identifying: what stays local and sharing.
- `scripting`: Use wgsextract from scripts and AI agents.
